text:
ops-ryan: Kicking off AP-SOUTHEAST-3 region bring-up. Primary ask: burn-in + stress plan for GPU pools, autoscale tuning, and final handoff checklist. Target launch window next Tue.
eng-ana: +1. Can we do a slow-bake ramp then a short high-stress spike? want to validate KV cache rehydration and prefix caching under load.
infra-jun: Plan suggestion: 3 phases — (1) warmup (priming images, caches), (2) steady ramp to target QPS, (3) 10-15m stress spike at 2x expected peak. We'll run these on dedicated test pool (not prod).
leah: Also include network flakiness sim — small packet drops and 200ms p95 latency to mimic inter-region egress. Did on eu test and caught a connection backoff bug.
pm-katie: For handoff, I need a one-page runbook for oncall + SRE with rollback steps and cost estimate if we keep extra capacity for 24h.
sre-bot: reminder: set incident channel #incidents-ap3 and enable auto-alert on GPUUtil>85% for >5m.
ops-ryan: Autoscale tuning idea: use a hybrid policy — primary metric tokens_per_sec per GPU, fallback to queue_depth. Set scale-up threshold at 75% tokens_per_sec and scale-down at 40%. What do you all think?
eng-ana: tokens_per_sec is fine but measure steady-state tail latency as guardrail. If p99 token latency > 250ms, pause rollouts and throttle traffic.
infra-jun: Suggested HPA-like snippet for k8s nodegroup scaling (for reference):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: infer-worker-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: infer-worker
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 64
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
```
ops-ryan: We're not just CPU — we'll hook a custom metric exporter for tokens_per_sec and queue_depth. autoscaler will use that.
leah: Load tooling: use vegeta for steady ramp and hey for spike. Example commands: `vegeta attack -rate 200 -duration 30m | vegeta report` and `hey -z 2m -c 500 http://ap3-test/infer`
eng-ana: Don't forget to prime KV cache: run a batch of representative prefix requests before any spike: script `scripts/prime_kv.sh` (will push 50k prefixes). Otherwise first-run latency will be horrid.
infra-jun: Cost note: if we keep reserved warm nodes for 6h it's approx $1.2k. If on-demand autoscale starts from 0 -> warm nodes we save money but risk cold-start tail latency. Pick strategy per customer tier.
pm-katie: For enterprise customers we should warm to at least 30% baseline capacity during launch window. Add that to handoff doc.
sre-bot: checklists created: `ap3-burnin-checklist.md` and `ap3-handoff.md` linked to runbook repo.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: infra/scale-config@deploy-1976543300 started.
ops-ryan: Observability: dashboards to confirm during runs — GPU utilization, tokens/sec per GPU, p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue depth, dropped requests, kv-cache hit ratio. Share dashboards 1h before run.
eng-ana: For tuning: if scale-ups lag > 90s, lower scale threshold by 5% or increase scale-step. Avoid oscillation by setting cooldown 180s.
leah: Network tests: use tc netem profile `netem-ap3.json` to inject 1% packet loss and 180ms delay. Run for 10m during spike.
infra-jun: Final handoff bullets for oncall: how to rollback (traffic-sieve back to eu1), how to drain ap3 worker nodes, how to pin model variant to quantized fallback. Also include cost kill-switch: if spend > $X/hour, auto-scale to baseline.
pm-katie: I'll consolidate and share the 1-pager. can one of you pair with me on the handoff doc review tomorrow?
eng-ana: I can do the review at 10am.
ops-ryan: Timeline: Mon — infra prep + dashboards, Tue AM — warmup + priming, Tue midday — ramp to steady, Tue PM — stress spike + network-fuzz, Tue evening — decision and handoff.
leah: Quick question — what GPU pool sizes? target is 24 A100-ish GPUs for initial capacity, can scale to 96 for spikes.
infra-jun: We'll provision a 32-GPU test pool and a gating 64-GPU launch pool. We'll leave autoscale max at 128 to be safe.
ops-ryan: Post-run tasks: collect eval prompts, check hallucination rates, and run quality regression on 1k sample prompts. Flag regressions to applied-ml.
pm-katie: ok thanks — please post the final runbook link and confirm participants on the handoff doc. :thumbsup:
eng-ana: Added small TODO: add health-check for NVLINK errors and driver OOM events. Those are silent but fatal.
ops-ryan: Great. If no objections I'll kick off infra/scale-config deploy at 09:00 UTC Mon and post a countdown.
leah: Sounds good.
pm-katie: Thanks everyone.
